name: Punto music

narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Elegant Intermission: Panama's Punto
This is Punto music. 19th century.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Title card: Punto music · Panama · 19th century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The punto is of pure Hispanic ancestry and is considered the most beautiful and elegant dance genre in Panama.
The accordion was introduced to the region in the mid-19th century by European sailors and became a common substitute for the violin during the War of the Thousand Days.
on_screen: Map: Panama · Central America
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: It is a demonstration of skill, precision, and grace.
It is not a dance for an entire night but a performance for the enjoyment of the audience, who may applaud or toss coins to show appreciation.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Blessed We Are (https://archive.org/details/guacamayo-danit-friends-live-2019)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance begins with the man kneeling on his left knee.
The couple then cycles through four movements: El Paseo (a wide circle), El Zapateo (face-to-face footwork), El Escobillao (a backward-moving separation), and El Seguidilla (close rotation).
Watch for El Paseo, El Zapateo.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Circular; man moves outside the circle in Punto de Mejorana
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The ensemble typically includes a rabel (folk fiddle) or accordion, a mejoranera or Spanish guitar, and drums (tambor repicador and tambor pujador).
The music is characterized by a 6/8 time signature and a ternary subdivision.
Listen for the rabel, accordion, mejoranera, flamenco guitar.
The pulse is 6/8.
A rustic, melodic fiddle or accordion leads over a ternary-subdivided rhythmic base provided by folk drums and chordophones.

narration: The dance is performed as an intermission at parties or social events.
Women may perform flourishes with their skirts, particularly in the Punto de Mejorana.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Variants include Punto Santeño (most popular), Punto Ocueño (free-style zapateo), Puntos of Chorrera (including Punto de Diablos), Punto de Salon, Punto de Parita, Punto de Mejorana, and Punto costeño.

music_brief.purpose: original soundtrack faithful to the tradition, with documented commercial reuse rights and no recurring royalties
music_brief.rights_rule: A composition brief does not clear an output. Record the provider/model/version, terms and date, input rights, output licence, restrictions and review before release.
music_brief.sound_description: A rustic, melodic fiddle or accordion leads over a ternary-subdivided rhythmic base provided by folk drums and chordophones.
music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Punto music (Panama). Meter 6/8. Instruments: rabel, accordion, mejoranera, flamenco guitar, tambor repicador, tambor pujador, caja redoblante. Form: melodic cantilena with ternary subdivision. Mood: elegant, graceful, passionate. It should sound like this: A rustic, melodic fiddle or accordion leads over a ternary-subdivided rhythmic base provided by folk drums and chordophones. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.

wardrobe.policy: the narrator wears the dance's traditional apparel, reconstructed meticulously and respectfully from the sources
wardrobe.from_sources: The dance is performed as an intermission at parties or social events. Women may perform flourishes with their skirts, particularly in the Punto de Mejorana.
care: every element traceable to the costume notes or a licensed image; nothing added for effect
no caricature, no exaggeration, no mixing of regions or eras
a culture bearer reviews the wardrobe before production; the review is recorded in the pack
credits name the tradition and the sources of the reconstruction
